properties.summary: Incident Type: STORAGE TANK - NRC Report ID: 1169598 - Medium Affected: WATER - Suspected Responsible Party: BURBANK WATER & POWER
properties.content:
Report Details

Incident Time: 2017-01-15 12:12:00
Nearest City: Burbank, CA
Location: 164 WEST MAGNOLIA BLVD.
Incident Type: STORAGE TANK
Material: SULFURIC ACID
Medium Affected: WATER
Suspected Responsible Party: BURBANK WATER & POWER
SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 34.177832, -118.316696 (Approximated from premise)
Reported Spill Volume: 5000 gallon
Report Description
ON 15JAN2017, SULFURIC ACID (93%) RELEASED FROM A STORAGE TANK. THIS WAS DUE TO THE DETERIORATION OF A FLANGE LINE, WHICH ERODED THE SURFACE AND THE ACID REACHED THE GASKETS. THIS RESULTED IN THE CATASTROPHIC FAILURE OF THE GASKET SEAL. AN ESTIMATED 5,000 GALLONS OF ACID RELEASED INTO THE SECONDARY CONTAINMENT SYSTEM. HOWEVER, CONTAINMENT WAS BREACHED AND 3,800 RELEASED ONTO THE GROUND, ASPHALT AND AROUND THE ZLD UNIT. A MINISCULE AMOUNT IS BELIEVED TO HAVE IMPACTED A STORM DRAIN. THE STORM WATER DISCHARGE RUNS INTO THE BURBANK WESTERN CHANNEL, BUT THERE IS NO KNOWN IMPACT (TESTING UNDERWAY).

Report Description///NOAA/NESDIS MPSR ISSUED FOR: GULF OF MEXICO/// A POSSIBLE OIL ANOMALY WAS OBSERVED IN SATELLITE IMAGERY. THIS ANOMALY IS UNCONFIRMED AS OIL. REPORT DATE: 09-28-2021 REPORT TIME: 0200 UTC REGION: GULF OF MEXICO SUB REGION: N/A AREA/BLOCK: HIGH ISLAND 129 IMAGE DATE: 09-28-2021 IMAGE TIME: 0015 UTC DATA SOURCE: RADARSAT2 MODE: STANDARD VV RESOLUTION: 25 METER LOCATION: 29°16"19" N/93°47"05" W AREA: 2.80 SQUARE KILOMETERS CONFIDENCE: HIGH REMARKS: POSSIBLE OIL WAS OBSERVED IN SATELLITE IMAGERY. THIS ANOMALY IS UNCONFIRMED AS OIL. THE ANOMALY HAD A HIGH CONTRAST TO ITS OTHERWISE HOMOGENEOUS SURROUNDINGS, AND IT HAD ABRUPT TURNS. THERE WERE TWO POSSIBLE OIL FACILITIES FROM WHICH THE ANOMALY APPEARED TO ORIGINATE. THE ANOMALY MEASURED APPROXIMATELY 5.9 NMI LONG IN TOTAL AND APPROXIMATELY 0.28 NMI WIDE AT ITS WIDEST POINT. WINDS NEAR THE TIME OF THE IMAGE WERE FROM THE SOUTHEAST AT 10 KTS, WHICH ORIENTED WELL WITH THE DIRECTION OF THE ANOMALY. UNCERTAINTIES: THERE MAY BE ADDITIONAL OIL IN THE AREA, ESPECIALLY TO THE NORTH, THAT IS VERY THIN AND APPEARS LIGHT IN SHADE IN THE SATELLITE IMAGE. THE DETACHED SLICKS ALSO APPEARED MORE DIFFUSE AT TIMES. AS PREVIOUSLY MENTIONED, THERE ARE TWO POSSIBLE POINT SOURCES, SO THERE IS SOME UNCERTAINTY WHERE EXACTLY THE ANOMALY APPEARED TO ORIGINATE.

////WEB REPORT///// CERCLA CONTINUOUS RELEASE REPORT [40CFR302.8(C)(1)] FOR AMMONIA SLIP STREAM RELEASED FROM THE REFINERY MAIN STACK (EMISSION POINT P-1). THE AQUEOUS AMMONIA IS INJECTED IN THE CO CRUDE FURNACES FOR NOX CONTROL TO MEET A TITLE V PERMIT LIMIT. THE AMMONIA SLIP STREAM WAS ESTIMATED USING SOURCE TEST DATA (5 POINTS). THE ESTIMATED DAILY RELEASE OF AMMONIA IS ABOUT 2,200 LBS/DAY WHICH IS IN EXCESS OF THE REPORTABLE QUANTITY (RQ) OF 100 LBS/DAY FOR CERCLA. PURSUANT TO 40CFR302.8(B), THIS RELEASE IS "CONTINUOUS" MEANING IT OCCURS WITHOUT INTERRUPTION (WHILE THE EQUIPMENT IS OPERATING) OR ABATEMENT OR THAT IT IS ROUTINE, ANTICIPATED, AND INTERMITTENT AND INCIDENTAL TO NORMAL OPERATIONS OR TREATMENT PROCESSES. THE VALERO BENICIA REFINERY IS A PETROLEUM PROCESSING FACILITY. THE MAIN STACK EMISSIONS POINT P-1 IS THE TALLEST STACK WITHIN THE FACILITY, AND IT IS THE FINAL RELEASE POINT FOR FLUE GAS FROM SEVERAL UPSTREAM PROCESSING UNITS, INCLUDING THE CRUDE CO FURNACES WHERE THE AQUEOUS AMMONIA IS INJECTED FOR NOX CONTROL TO MEET A TITLE V PERMIT LIMIT.

Reported Spill Volume: 1583000 gallon
Report DescriptionREPORT RECEIVED FROM NATIONAL COMMAND CENTER: THIS IS A POTENTIAL RELEASE... COAST GUARD SECTOR LOS ANGELES/LONG BEACH INITIATED A CIC FOR THE M/V PRESIDENT EISENHOWER (FLAG: US) THAT EXPERIENCED AN ENGINE FIRE AND CURRENTLY ADRIFT OFFSHORE OF SANTA BARBARA, CA. THE M/V PRESIDENT EISENHOWER IS A 943 FT, US FLAG GENERAL CARGO VESSEL WITH 22 POB, WITH NO REPORTED INJURIES. THE VESSEL ACTIVATED THE CO2 FIRE SUPPRESSION SYSTEM AND SHIP COMPANY HAS MADE ARRANGEMENT FOR A TUG ASSIST WITH AN ETA OF 4HRS (1500 PDT). THE M/V REMAINS DISABLED AND ADRIFT 10NM SOUTH OF SANTA BARBARA BUT WITHIN CLOSE PROXIMITY TO OIL PLATFORM HONDO WHICH HAS 25 PERSON. THERE MAY BE POSSIBLE ALLISON BETWEEN THE VESSEL AND THE OIL PLATFORM. CALCULATED DRIFT IS AT 1 KNOT AND CLOSEST POINT OF APPROACH IS CALCULATED AT 1NM. SECTOR LOS ANGELES/LONG BEACH IS IN COMMUNICATION WITH BOTH THE VESSEL AND THE OIL PLATFORM. THERE IS A VESSEL ON STANDBY TO EVACUATE THE PERSONNEL FROM THE OIL PLATFORM IF NEEDED. POTENTIAL POLLUTION IS 1.57 MILLION GALLONS OF DIESEL/FUEL COMBO ON THE VESSEL AND 13,000 GALLONS OF DIESEL ON THE OIL PLATFORM. THERE IS NO MEDIA ATTENTION AT THIS TIME. A FOLLOW-ON CIC WILL BE HELD AT 2015 ZULU (1315 PDT/1615 EST) AN EARLIER NRC REPORT NUMBER 1303658 WAS GENERATED WITH PRELIMINARY INFORMATION REGARDING THE INCIDENT.
